title: How can one known product answer four calculations?
description: A hundred and fifty six times twelve is one thousand eight hundred and seventy two. That one fact answers a product, a quotient, another quotient and a product with small decimals, by ignoring the decimal point and then counting decimal places. Multiplying back checks one answer.
teaching_notes: One idea: use the known digits and place the decimal point by counting places, or by scaling both numbers in a division alike. Watch for students who lose the zero in front of the digits in the last product.

video_script.why: The child knows a hundred and fifty six times twelve but does not see how it answers calculations with decimals.
video_script.substitution: Products keep the digits and count decimal places; quotients scale both numbers alike until they match the known fact.
video_script.anchor: A hundred and fifty six times twelve is one thousand eight hundred and seventy two, used for four calculations
video_script.payoff_line: The last answer is zero point zero one eight seven two.

final_answer.spoken: eighteen point seven two, a hundred and fifty six, one point two and zero point zero one eight seven two

video_script.design: The known fact stays on the board; each of the four calculations is turned into the digits of the fact and the decimal point is placed by counting places or scaling.

beats.on_screen: title card From your book; the fact 156 × 12 = 1872 at the top; four calculations below it: 15.6 × 1.2, 187.2 ÷ 1.2, 18.72 ÷ 15.6, 0.156 × 0.12, each with an empty box

marks.fact: the known fact appears at the top

narration: <bookmark mark='scene'/>This is a question from your book about using a known fact.
<bookmark mark='fact'/>We know a hundred and fifty six times twelve is one thousand eight hundred and seventy two.
<bookmark mark='ab'/>The first is fifteen point six times one point two. The second is a hundred and eighty seven point two divided by one point two.
<bookmark mark='cd'/>The third is eighteen point seven two divided by fifteen point six. The fourth is zero point one five six times zero point one two.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>What are the four answers?

beats.on_screen: the fact, the four calculations and their empty boxes stay on the board

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: The fact 156 × 12 = 1872 is kept; products keep the digits and count decimal places; divisions scale both numbers alike

marks.same: the digits one eight seven two are kept on the board
marks.prod: an arrow shows the decimal places being counted for a product
marks.div: an arrow shows both numbers of a division being scaled alike

narration: <bookmark mark='same'/>We solve this the same way as the example in your book. We keep the digits of the known fact.
<bookmark mark='prod'/>For a product, count the decimal places in both numbers to place the point.
<bookmark mark='div'/>For a division, multiply both numbers by ten or a hundred, until they match the fact.
<bookmark mark='given'/>Given, a hundred and fifty six times twelve is one thousand eight hundred and seventy two.

beats.on_screen: To find: the four answers using the fact

marks.find: the four answer boxes are outlined

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find the four answers by using this fact.

marks.s1b: the decimal point in each number is ignored and 156 × 12 = 1872 is matched
marks.s1c: two decimal places are counted and the decimal point is placed to give 18.72

narration: <bookmark mark='s1a'/>Step one, fifteen point six times one point two.
<bookmark mark='s1b'/>Ignore the decimal point in each number. A hundred and fifty six times twelve is one thousand eight hundred and seventy two.
<bookmark mark='s1c'/>Each number has one decimal place, so the answer has two. That gives eighteen point seven two.

marks.s2b: both numbers are multiplied by 10 to give 1872 ÷ 12

narration: <bookmark mark='s2a'/>Step two, a hundred and eighty seven point two divided by one point two.
<bookmark mark='s2b'/>Multiply both numbers by ten. We get one thousand eight hundred and seventy two divided by twelve.
<bookmark mark='s2c'/>A hundred and fifty six times twelve is one thousand eight hundred and seventy two. That means the answer is a hundred and fifty six.

marks.s3b: both numbers are multiplied by 10 to give 187.2 ÷ 156

narration: <bookmark mark='s3a'/>Step three, eighteen point seven two divided by fifteen point six.
<bookmark mark='s3b'/>Multiply both numbers by ten. We get a hundred and eighty seven point two divided by a hundred and fifty six.
<bookmark mark='s3c'/>One thousand eight hundred and seventy two divided by a hundred and fifty six is twelve.
<bookmark mark='s3d'/>Divide twelve by ten, and we get one point two.

marks.s4b: the decimal point in each number is ignored and the digits 1872 are matched
marks.s4c: five decimal places are counted and five empty places are drawn after the decimal point

narration: <bookmark mark='s4a'/>Step four, zero point one five six times zero point one two.
<bookmark mark='s4b'/>Ignore the decimal point in each number. The digits one eight seven two come from the known fact.
<bookmark mark='s4c'/>Three decimal places and two decimal places make five. Write the digits with five places, which needs a zero in front.

marks.s5b: the product 187.2 is matched with the number in 187.2 ÷ 1.2

narration: <bookmark mark='s5a'/>Step five, check the second answer by multiplying back. A hundred and fifty six times one point two is a hundred and eighty seven point two.
<bookmark mark='s5b'/>That matches the number we began with.

marks.rest: the other three answers are boxed

narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>The last answer is zero point zero one eight seven two.
<bookmark mark='rest'/>The other three are eighteen point seven two, a hundred and fifty six, and one point two.
